# Full active-menu optimization for the smooth singleton-source problem

This note keeps ALL active base tilts at every actual positive-width singleton source. A fixed selected menu does not exhaust this information. The resulting source-loss functional is a maximum over balanced menus, not a fixed linear functional. Its exact quantifiers clarify both the descent alternative and the dependence of the separator on menu selection.

Dependencies: the attained smooth body problem, uniform own source cores, exact finite clipping, the actual physical cone, and the singleton cover construction in
\`candidate 0fa64553cd01d7ae\`.
No new sharp numerical efficiency theorem is assumed.

## 1. Compact active caps and the correct menu measure

Fix an actual smooth body minimum at positive parameters \(\epsilon,h\), with total mass \(M\), maximal raw depth \(Q=M\beta\), and singleton sources \(Y_i=(p_i,y_i)\). Write \(f_i=f_H(Y_i)\). Normalize every active continuous normal by \(\Gamma(u)=1\).

For source \(i\), let \(\mathcal A_i\) be a compact set of representatives of ALL its active caps, including all their possible base tilts. Such representatives exist by exact finite clipping. That clipping keeps every nonsaturated fiber margin fixed and keeps the remaining smooth integrands saturated. It consequently preserves not only cap mass but also the boundary profile, strip coarea and strip first-margin moment used below. It also preserves the first body response for every bounded physical field. Thus no response is lost by taking compact representatives.

For \(N=(a,u)\in\mathcal A_i\), put
\[
c_N=N\cdot Y_i-\epsilon f_i,\quad
q_N(w)=(N\cdot w-c_N)/h,
\]
\[
S_N=\int\psi(q_N)\,d\mu/h>0,\qquad
A_N=\int q_N\psi(q_N)\,d\mu,\qquad
g_N=S_N(u-\epsilon\nabla_x f_i).
\]
These are continuous in the cap parameters. The fixed positive width and own core give uniform upper and positive lower bounds for \(S_N\).

Define
\[
\mathcal M_i=
\left\{\text{Borel probabilities }\nu\text{ on }\mathcal A_i:
              \int g_N\,d\nu(N)=0\right\}. \tag{1}
\]
This is a nonempty compact convex set. Nonemptiness follows from the actual own-fiber first-order active-normal balance. Its measures are the NORMALIZED RESPONSE weights, rather than the raw quantile weights.

For comparison, a quantile menu has a probability \(\rho\) satisfying
\(\int u\,d\rho=\epsilon\nabla_x f_i\). Its response measure is
\[
d\nu=\frac{S_N^{-1}d\rho}{\int S_N^{-1}d\rho}.
\]
Conversely \(d\rho=S_Nd\nu/\int S_Nd\nu\). Thus (1) includes precisely all balanced coarea-weighted menus. In particular different active base tilts having the same continuous normal remain distinct caps and may be selected independently.

## 2. Exact through-source loss and optimized source loss

Let \(\Phi\) be any actual signed normal-dependent convex physical field, with inward speed \(v\) on the old normal bundle. Let \(D=\int v\,d\sigma\), \(\dot f_i\) be the actual tied-profile response at the fixed source, and \(\dot\Gamma_N\) its actual covariance-norm response, with the cap normal held fixed. All are linear in the physical field.

The cap at its moving through-source threshold has raw loss
\[
L_{i,N}(\Phi)
 =\int_{\partial S}\Psi(q_N)v\,d\sigma
   -\epsilon S_N\dot f_i+(A_N-\epsilon f_iS_N)\dot\Gamma_N.
\tag{2}
\]
Indeed the threshold derivative is
\(-\epsilon\dot f_i-\epsilon f_i\dot\Gamma_N\), and the separate smoothing-width response is \(A_N\dot\Gamma_N\). Formula (2) retains that width term.

If the source mark is given continuous velocity \(z\), its first-order cap loss changes by \(g_N\cdot z\). Hence the candidate optimized raw source loss is
\[
\mathcal L_i(\Phi)=
 \inf_{z\in\mathbb R^d}\max_{N\in\mathcal A_i}
       [L_{i,N}(\Phi)+g_N\cdot z].
\tag{3}
\]
The exact finite-dimensional dual identity is
\[
\mathcal L_i(\Phi)=
 \max_{\nu\in\mathcal M_i}\int L_{i,N}(\Phi)\,d\nu(N).
\tag{4}
\]

For a direct proof, take the compact convex hull of the vectors
\((g_N,L_{i,N})\) in \(\mathbb R^{d+1}\). The right side is the highest last coordinate over first coordinate zero. Every affine upper plane \(t+z\cdot g\leq b\) bounds that value, giving one direction of (4). Conversely a point \((0,b)\) strictly above the compact convex hull can be strictly separated from it. Comparison with a point of that hull having first coordinate zero forces the last-coordinate coefficient of this separator to be positive. Normalize it to one; its remaining coefficients give a finite \(z\) for which the maximum in (3) is below \(b\). Let \(b\) decrease to the right side. This proves (4) even when the infimum in (3) is not attained.

The maximum in (4) is attained, and it has a representative supported on at most \(d+1\) active caps. To see this without a measure-extremality assertion, apply ordinary Caratheodory in \(\mathbb R^{d+1}\) to a maximizing vector \((0,\mathcal L_i)\), obtaining at most \(d+2\) caps. If \(d+2\) positive weights remain, there is a nonzero perturbation preserving their sum and the \(d\) first coordinates. Both signs are feasible for sufficiently small perturbations. Maximality forces its last-coordinate variation to vanish. Move to an endpoint where one weight vanishes, leaving at most \(d+1\).

## 3. Why this is the actual directional derivative

For a fixed finite mark velocity \(z\), the smooth cap expansion is uniform over the compact representative set. The uniform kernel gives the needed \(C^1\) plane dependence because its two kink planes have zero mixed volume. The bounded physical speeds and continuous boundary capture factors give uniform first shape response by dominated convergence and compactness. The usual active-set envelope argument therefore gives the first-order depth at the trial mark \(Y_i+t(0,z)\) as
\[
Q-t\max_{N\in\mathcal A_i}
 [L_{i,N}(\Phi)+g_N\cdot z]+o(t).
\]
Taking finite approximate minimizers in (3) proves the lower bound for the optimized source depth.

For the matching upper bound, choose a maximizing finite menu in (4), convert it to its quantile weights \(\rho\), and use its ACTUAL smooth covering continuation from the companion note. Its unique old contact is the source, and its contact minimum has the proved first expansion. Exact quantile equalization gives source-fiber upper bound
\(Q-t\int L_{i,N}\,d\nu+o(t)\).
This proves that the actual optimized raw depth on the \(p_i\)-fiber has derivative \(-\mathcal L_i(\Phi)\). No assumption that maximizing marks move at speed \(O(t)\) is needed for this upper argument.

Define normalized improvement
\[
G_i(\Phi)=\mathcal L_i(\Phi)-\beta D.
\tag{5}
\]
The finite off-source gap persists. Therefore the actual global normalized objective has one-sided derivative
\[
\left.\frac{d}{dt}\beta(K_t)\right|_{0+}
=-\frac1M\min_i G_i(\Phi).
\tag{6}
\]
Every \(G_i\) is a maximum of linear functionals on the physical cone, hence is convex and positively homogeneous. It should not be replaced by the concave branch minimum from the earlier unsmoothed contact problem.

## 4. Exact menu/field/minimum quantifiers

An actual attained body minimum satisfies
\[
\forall\Phi\text{ in the actual cone},\qquad
\min_i\max_{\nu\in\mathcal M_i}
 \left[\int L_{i,N}(\Phi)\,d\nu-\beta D\right]\leq0.
\tag{7}
\]
Conversely, finding one field for which every displayed group maximum is strictly positive gives an ACTUAL first-order descent. Only that direction is needed; (7) is not a sufficient condition for a body minimum.

Since the source menus may be chosen independently and their maxima are attained, (7) is equivalent to:
for EVERY complete selection \((\nu_i)_i\), there is no physical field making all of its selected linear improvements positive. The quantifiers are
\[
\forall(\nu_i)_i\ \forall\Phi\quad
 \min_i G_{i,\nu_i}(\Phi)\leq0. \tag{8}
\]
For each fixed complete selection, separation on finite physical cones and compactness of the source-weight simplex give ONE coherent separator \(\lambda\) for all fields. But this \(\lambda\) may depend on the complete menu selection.

There is no valid automatic interchange
\(\forall\text{ menus }\exists\lambda\) with
\(\exists\lambda\forall\text{ menus}\).
For an exact scalar model take two improvement-coefficient sets
\([1,2]\) and \([-2,-1]\), tested on the signed line of fields \(t\in\mathbb R\). For every selected pair \(a>0>b\), a convex mixture makes the coefficient zero, and neither sign of \(t\) makes both group improvements positive. No single mixture weight balances ALL pairs \(a,b\). Thus the menu-dependence is a real logical issue, even with compact convex menu sets.

## 5. A concrete favorable-menu exposure criterion

Let \(q\) be an exposed vertex of the COMPLETE base hull. For source \(i\), restrict \(\mathcal A_i\) to caps whose smooth capture is identically one on the entire \(q\)-fiber. Such caps support a balanced menu exactly when zero lies in the convex hull of their \(g_N\)'s; equivalently \(\epsilon\nabla_x f_i\) lies in the convex hull of their normalized continuous normals.

If this holds, select that menu. An actual nonnegative convex field can isolate the \(q\)-fiber with positive boundary integral, as in the exposed-base transfer note. Its selected capture profile is one on that support.

More generally, suppose for EACH source there is such an exposed target \(q_i\). Use one normalized isolating field for each distinct target and sum them. If there are \(r\) distinct targets, then the total boundary integral is \(r\), while each source's selected capture integral is at least one. The own-energy and own-volume response terms have the favorable sign, the covariance coefficients are nonnegative, and the remaining uniform tied-buffer/width errors are at most \(C(\epsilon+h)\) times the boundary integral. Consequently every group improves when
\[
\beta+C(\epsilon+h)<1/r.
\]
Here \(r\leq |I|\leq k(P)\). Thus this criterion excludes an actual low-depth smooth minimum for sufficiently small parameters below \(\Gamma_d/k(P)\).

This is a proved sufficient exposure/descent criterion. It does not assert that its restricted active-normal hull condition holds for an arbitrary source. The exact interior triangle-product example DOES satisfy it: keep the orbit of its continuous minimizing directions but assign all their base tilts to capture the SAME outer vertex. This menu pays, even though a different simultaneous menu was proved nonpaying.

The general best-active-menu \(\Gamma_d\) efficiency assertion remains a theorem-strength missing step until proved or refuted. The present note supplies its correct optimization domain and quantifiers, rather than assuming it.
